newsitem.title: USA: Ice storm glazes U.S. Great Plains.
newsitem.headline: Ice storm glazes U.S. Great Plains.

text.p: Freezing rain coated streets and highways with a dangerous layer of ice across the Great Plains Friday, causing at least one traffic death and closing some schools, authorities said.
A semi-trailer truck crashed early Friday on Interstate 90 near Plankinton, S.D., resulting in one death, officials said.
"There have been a number of accidents, which you would expect with the first icing of the season," said Jeff Chapman of the National Weather Service in nearby Sioux Falls.

Freezing rain began during Thursday's evening rush hour and swept across parts of the Dakotas, Iowa, Wisconsin and Minnesota, glazing trees and power lines and knocking out electricity to some residents. Farther west in Colorado's skiing areas, up to six inches of snow was forecast as a series of storm fronts moved eastward.

In Minneapolis, more than an inch of sleet turned roads icy, causing more than 100 traffic accidents at a rate of one every two minutes Friday, the highway patrol said. There were no serious injuries. Scores of Northwest Airlines flights were cancelled or delayed at the carrier's Minneapolis hub.

In snowbound northern Ohio, authorities appealed to residents to clear blocked gutters and sewers of leaves as this week's early-season snowfall melted as temperatures rose. Many schools opened for the first time this week.
Chardon, a suburb east of Cleveland along Lake Erie, received a record 69 inches of snow through Thursday and rain was forecast for the weekend.
A powerful low pressure system in the Atlantic, which was lashing Florida with high winds, was expected to slow the eastward flow of the storms.
